claim.title: Underparametrized Risk Divergence
claim.statement: In the underparametrized regime (γ < 1), the prediction risk of the min-norm least squares estimator diverges to infinity as γ approaches 1 from below.
claim.test_plan: Simulate isotropic model with n=1000. Compute min-norm risk for γ in [0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999]. Verify that the risk increases as γ increases towards 1. Pass if Risk(0.999) > Risk(0.99) > Risk(0.95) > Risk(0.9) and Risk(0.999) > 10 * Risk(0.9).
claim.success_criterion: The risk at γ=0.999 is greater than 10 times the risk at γ=0.9, and the risk is monotonically increasing with γ in the range [0.9, 0.999].

feedback: Transferred from the arxiv-1912.07242 audit round: Monte-Carlo audits at d=1000 timed out 3x within the 20-min bound; d<=300 (T<=300 trials, focused grids around critical points) gave statistically clean verdicts in minutes. Design for that envelope. Asymptotic closed-forms converge quickly in d — a large-d run is wasted budget, not better evidence.
